newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on NWS weather forecast.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on NWS weather forecast.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a forecast for nearly ideal crop weather to continue in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

The National Weather Service Wednesday, in its six- to 10-day outlook, predicted the U.S. Midwest would experience below normal temperatures and above normal rainfall July 15-19. That scenario would be nearly perfect for the U.S. corn crop which is entering its critical pollination or reproductive stage of development.
The sentiment was a departure from Wednesday, when corn futures rallied on talk some private forecasters were calling for hotter and drier weather over the near term in the Midwest.

Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio early Thursday said the Midwest should remain cool and mostly dry for the next couple of days, ahead of showers expected to move across the region this weekend.
Corn closed unchanged to 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down two at $2.47-3/4. New crop December closed 2-3/4 lower at $2.34-1/2.
However, declines were curbed in corn futures by a neutral to supportive government export sales report.

USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended July 3 totalled 477,300 tonnes for old crop, within the range of expectations for 450,000 to 550,000 tonnes. Net export sales of new crop totalled 395,400 tonnes, also within the range of expectations for 350,000 to 450,000 tonnes.
Refco Inc sold five million bushels of December, Continental Grain sold 2.5 million bushels of Dec and R.J. O'Brien sold 1.5 million bushels of Dec, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services bought five million bushels of December, Lind Waldock bought 2.5 million bushels of Dec and Tenco Inc bought two million bushels of Dec, traders said.
In spread trading, Tenco Inc did 1.5 million bushels of July/December at 12-1/2 to 13-1/2 cents and Hagarty Trading spread 1.5 million July/December at 12-1/2 to 13-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 40,000 contracts, below the 70,083 traded Wednesday.

In corn options, Lind Waldock bought 1,000 December $2.50 puts at 22 cents and sold 1,000 December $2.30 puts at nine cents, traders said. Cargill Investor Services bought 1,000 December $2.30 puts at 8-3/4 cents, floor sources added.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, below the 24,230 traded Wednesday.
